subject: Hashchain verification and statement on data integrity
messages:
From: Claire Nguyen <claire.nguyen@clearwavehealth.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.inference>
Cc: security@clearwavehealth.com
Date: Fri, 07 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Request: chain-of-custody and hash verification for May 1-3 window

Jonas,

Thanks for the quick sync earlier. Clearwave's security team is requesting a cryptographic record we can include in our internal audit: a hashchain or signed digests for the inference-runtime logs covering 2027-05-01 00:00:00 UTC to 2027-05-03 23:59:59 UTC, plus a short technical statement confirming whether any customer data was read, copied, or exported during that window.

Please include:
- A manifest of the log files / indices and their SHA-256 (or HMAC-SHA256) digests
- A short description of the verification method (how snaps were taken, signing key used, and who performed verification)
- Any sampling methodology and results if you did not run a full-file hash for every file
- A statement suitable for our audit saying whether any customer records were accessed or exfiltrated

We will need the attestation in a form that can be shared with our compliance team (PDF or DocuSign preferred). If you need an approval or POC contact on our side, cc: legal@clearwavehealth.com.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — can you aim to share the artifacts today?

Thanks,
Claire Nguyen
Security Program Manager
Clearwave Health

From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.inference>
To: Claire Nguyen <claire.nguyen@clearwavehealth.com>
Cc: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.inference>, evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.inference>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 07 May 2027 09:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: chain-of-custody and hash verification for May 1-3 window

Hi Claire — thanks for the detailed list. We're on it. Summary of next steps from our side: 

1) Evelyn (security) will run a chain verification across the inference-runtime-logs indices for the exact window you specified and produce a signed digest manifest.
2) We'll provide a short technical note that documents the HMAC signing key provenance, the verification script, and the sampling approach.
3) We'll produce a PDF attestation and can send via DocuSign if you prefer.

Attachments I'll drop into this thread: requested_data-range_manifest.csv (index names/time ranges) — internal draft.

Evelyn: can you confirm ETA? I told Claire we'd aim to deliver the artifacts within 4–5 hours.

Claire: if there's a specific person in legal who must countersign, please confirm so we can route the DocuSign correctly.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Director, Customer Security & Trust
Redwood Inference

From: evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.inference>

Cc: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.inference>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 07 May 2027 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: chain-of-custody and hash verification for May 1-3 window

Claire / team —

We completed the verification and are attaching the artifacts. Summary (technical):

- Scope: All shards of indices prefixed with "inference-runtime-logs" for time window 2027-05-01T00:00:00Z through 2027-05-03T23:59:59Z.
- Method: A snapshot was taken from node-level read-only copies. For each log file we computed file-level SHA-256 digests and then produced an HMAC-SHA256 over the ordered digest list (HMAC key stored in our KMS). All HMAC results were timestamped and persisted to a tamper-evident archive. Verification was performed by a pair of engineers (Evelyn Hart, Security; Marcus Lin, SRE) using the chain_verification.py script (attached).

Sample HMAC outputs (manifest excerpt):
- inference-runtime-logs-2027-05-01-shard-1: HMAC-SHA256 = 3f7a9b2a6c9d...b1e5 (full in attached CSV)
- inference-runtime-logs-2027-05-02-shard-4: HMAC-SHA256 = a2c1e9f4d0b8...7c3d
- inference-runtime-logs-2027-05-03-shard-2: HMAC-SHA256 = 9b8f3c1ae4d2...0a6f

Result: No integrity discrepancies were observed between the persisted snapshots and the verification run. We found no evidence of unauthorized read or export activity targeting customer records in the queried window. 

Formal attestation: Attached is a signed attestation (signed_attestation-20270507.pdf). The attestation includes a statement of scope, the signing principal (Evelyn Hart, Head of Security, Redwood Inference), and the canonical HMAC key id (kms://projects/redwood/keys/hash-verification-v2). We can route this via DocuSign per your preference — I included a draft sign-ready PDF in the attachments.

Attachments (in this thread):
- hash_digest_manifest-20270507.csv (full list of files and HMACs)
- chain_verification-script.log (execution log with checksum timestamps)
- signed_attestation-20270507.pdf (signed by security lead)
- chain_verification.py (utility used for verification)

If you want additional evidence (e.g., a PKI-signed timestamp from an external TSA, or logs showing the KMS key usage), we can generate that. Let me know which of the above would satisfy Clearwave's auditors.

Evelyn Hart
Head of Security, Redwood Inference
Evelyn.hart@redwood.inference
